clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the action_schema is the description of actions, the reasons for these actions, and the status of these actions.

example.p: Reasons for action include evolving user requirements, manufacturing problems and difficulties that arise when a product is in use.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: Action information can be attached to any aspect of product data.

clause.title: supported_item
clause.p:
The supported_item allows for the designation of an action_directiveaction_directive, an actionaction, or an action_methodaction_method.NOTENote4.3.5, Note
This specifies the use of an action_resourceaction_resource.

clause.title: action
clause.p: An action is the identification of the occurrence of an activity and a description of its result.
An action identifies an activity that has taken place, is taking place, or is expected to take place in the future.

An action has a definition that is specified by an action_methodaction_method.NOTE 1Note 14.4.1, Note 1
In particular application domains, terms such as task, process, activity, operation, and event may be synonyms for action.

example.p: Change, distilling, design, a process to drill a hole, and a task such as training someone are examples of actions.

dd.p: the labellabel by which the action is known.
the texttext that characterizes the action. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
the action_methodaction_method that specifies the procedure selected to carry out the action and a description of the results of that action.
the identifieridentifier that distinguishes the action.

note.p: This attribute is an enhancement to the definition of action using a method that is upwardly compatible with ISO 10303-41:1994.

The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

The context in which id is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.

dd.p: Each action shall be the identified_itemidentified_item in at most one id_attributeid_attribute.

note.p: The id_attributeid_attribute data type is defined in basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema of this part of ISO 10303.
A template for constraining the population of the entity data types defined in the basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema is described in annex E.

clause.title: action_directive
clause.p: An action_directive is an authoritative instrument that provides directions to achieve the specified results.

example.p: ISO Directives Part 3 provides guidance for the development of standards documents within ISO.

dd.p: the labellabel by which the action_directive is known.
the texttext that characterizes the action_directive. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

an informal description of the results of the analysis that was carried out on the elements of the requests set. The request sets are the versioned_action_requestversioned_action_requests referenced in the requests attribute.

note.p: The reason that different requests are satisfied by the action_directive could be recorded in this attribute.

dd.p: an informal description of any other pertinent information.
a set of versioned_action_requestversioned_action_request entity data types that defines the expected results.

clause.title: action_method
clause.p:
An action_method is the definition of an activity. This definition includes the activity’s objectives and effects.NOTENote4.4.3, Note
This definition may be the basis for actions or the solution for action requests.

example.p: For the actionaction whose name attribute is ‘serve dinner’, the name attribute of related instance of action_method could be ‘cook by recipe’ or ‘purchase takeout food’.

dd.p: the labellabel by which the action_method is known.
the texttext that characterizes the action_method. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
an informal description of the effects of the action_method.
an informal description of the objectives of the action_method.

clause.title: action_method_relationship
clause.p:
An action_method_relationship is a relationship between two instances of the entity data type action_methodaction_method and provides an identification and description of this relationship.NOTE 1Note 14.4.4, Note 1
The role of action_method_relationship can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 2Note 24.4.4, Note 2
This entity, together with the action_methodaction_method entity, is based on the relationship template that is described in annex E.3. NOTE 3Note 34.4.4, Note 3
This entity may be used to define a procedural relationship among constituent activities.

dd.p: the labellabel by which the action_method_relationship is known.
the texttext that characterizes the action_method_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
one of the instances of action_methodaction_method that is a part of the relationship.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the other instance of action_methodaction_method that is a part of the relationship. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other this attribute shall be the dependent one.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: action_relationship
clause.p:
An action_relationship is a relationship between two instances of the entity data type actionaction and provides an identification and description of this relationship.NOTE 1Note 14.4.5, Note 1
The role of action_relationship can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the labellabel by which the action_relationship is known.
the texttext that characterizes the action_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
one of the instances of actionaction that is a part of the relationship.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the other instance of actionaction that is a part of the relationship. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other this attribute shall be the dependent one.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: action_request_solution
clause.p: An action_request_solution is an association between a versioned_action_requestversioned_action_request and an action_methodaction_method that is a potential solution for the request.

dd.p: the action_methodaction_method that is a potential solution.
the versioned_action_requestversioned_action_request for which a solution is specified.
the texttext that characterizes the action_request_solution.

note.p: This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to action_request_solution as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994.

dd.p: the labellabel by which the action_request_solution is known.

note.p: This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to action_request_solution as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994.

dd.p: Each action_request_solution shall be the described_itemdescribed_item in at most one description_attributedescription_attribute.

note.p: The description_attributedescription_attribute data type is defined in basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema of this part of ISO 10303.

dd.p: Each action_request_solution shall be the named_itemnamed_item in at most one name_attributename_attribute.

note.p: The name_attributename_attribute data type is defined in basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema of this part of ISO 10303.
A template for constraining the population of the entity data types defined in the basic_attribute_schemabasic_attribute_schema is described in annex E.

clause.title: action_request_status
clause.p: An action_request_status is the association of a status with a versioned_action_requestversioned_action_request.

dd.p: the labellabel that provides a user interpretable designation for the level of completion of the action.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the versioned_action_requestversioned_action_request to which the status applies.

clause.title: action_resource
clause.p: An action_resource is a thing that is identified as being needed to carry out an action.

dd.p: the labellabel by which the action_resource is known.
the texttext that characterizes the action_resource. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
a set of supported_itemsupported_items for which the action_resource is used.
the action_resource_typeaction_resource_type that specifies the sort of action_resource that is being used.

clause.title: action_resource_relationship
clause.p:
An action_resource_relationship is a relationship between two instances of the entity data type action_resourceaction_resource and provides an identification and description of this relationship.NOTE 1Note 14.4.9, Note 1
The role of action_resource_relationship can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 2Note 24.4.9, Note 2
This entity, together with the action_resourceaction_resource entity, is based on the relationship template that is described in annex E.3.

dd.p: the labellabel by which the action_resource_relationship is known.
the texttext that characterizes the action_resource_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
one of the instances of action_resourceaction_resource that is a part of the relationship.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the other instance of action_resourceaction_resource that is a part of the relationship. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other this attribute shall be the dependent one.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: action_resource_type
clause.p: An action_resource_type is the identification of the kind of action_resourceaction_resource needed to carry out an action.

example.p: This entity may be used to specify the kind of tool needed to perform a process operation.

dd.p: the labellabel by which the action_resource_type is known.

clause.title: action_status
clause.p:
An action_status is the association of a status with an executed_actionexecuted_action.NOTE 1Note 14.4.11, Note 1
Information about the date and time may be associated with the action_status through the use of date_assignmentdate_assignment, date_and_time_assignmentdate_and_time_assignment, or time_assignmenttime_assignment.

dd.p: the labellabel that provides a user interpretable designation for the level of completion of the action.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

example.p: Terms such as ‘pending’, ‘completed’, or ‘scheduled’ are examples of status.

dd.p: the executed_actionexecuted_action to which the status applies.

clause.title: directed_action
clause.p: A directed_action is a type of executed_actionexecuted_action that is governed by an action_directiveaction_directive.

example.p: A directed_action could be the inspection of a building as directed by city officials according to the city building codes for earthquake safety. The action is the inspection of the building. The directive is issued by city officials guided by the city building codes. In an application protocol, the building authority may be associated with an organization_assignmentorganization_assignment. The building codes may be associated with a document_referencedocument_reference.

dd.p: the action_directiveaction_directive that governs the directed_action.

clause.title: directed_action_assignment
clause.p: A directed_action_assignment is an association of a directed_actiondirected_action with product data.

dd.p: the instance of the directed_action entity data that is to be associated with product data.
the object_role that specifies the purpose of the association of the directed_action_assignment with product data.
Each directed_action_assignment shall be item_with_role in at most one role_associationrole_association.

clause.title: executed_action
clause.p:
An executed_action is a type of actionaction that is completed, partially completed, or just identified. It may but need not have status information associated with it.NOTE 1Note 14.4.14, Note 1
The role of executed_action can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information. NOTE 2Note 24.4.14, Note 2
Status information is associated to executed_action through action_statusaction_status.

example.p: An executed_action could be to ‘paint the office’ with a status of ‘scheduled’. The action is ‘paint the office’. The status further qualifies the action as ‘planned’, ‘scheduled’, or ‘completed’.

clause.title: versioned_action_request
clause.p:
A versioned_action_request is a specification of a desired result.NOTE 1Note 14.4.15, Note 1
The desired result being identified and described may be obtained through one of more action_methodaction_methods.

dd.p: the identifieridentifier that distinguishes the versioned_action_request.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

The context in which id is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the identification of the version of the versioned_action_request. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
an informal description of the reason for the versioned_action_request.
the texttext that characterizes the versioned_action_request. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

clause.title: versioned_action_request_relationship
clause.p:
A versioned_action_request_relationship is a relationship between two versioned_action_requestversioned_action_request objects.NOTE 1Note 14.4.16, Note 1
Two versioned_action_requestversioned_action_request objects may be related if they address similar problems. NOTE 2Note 24.4.16, Note 2
A versioned_action_requestversioned_action_request may be a version of a work request. It might be related to a different version of the work request using a versioned_action_request_relationship.

dd.p: the identifieridentifier that distinguishes the versioned_action_request_relationship.
the labellabel by which the versioned_action_request_relationship is known.
the texttext that characterizes the versioned_action_request_relationship. The value of this attribute need not be specified.
one of the instances of versioned_action_requestversioned_action_request that is a part of the relationship.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the other instance of versioned_action_requestversioned_action_request that is a part of the relationship. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other, this attribute shall be the dependent one.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: action_directive_relationship
clause.p: An action_directive_relationship is a relationship between two action_directiveaction_directive objects.

dd.p: shall be unique within a population of action_directive_relationship.
the text or the set of texts that provide further information about the action_directive_relationship. The value of this attribute need not be specified.
one object of action_directiveaction_directive that is part of the relationship.
the other object of action_directiveaction_directive that is part of the relationship.
the meaning of the relationship.
A action_directive_relationship shall not participate in its own definition.

clause.title: acyclic_action_method_relationship
clause.p: The acyclic_action_method_relationship function determines whether the graph of instances of the entity data type action_methodaction_method that contains relation as one of its links contains a cycle. This function may be used to evaluate either an action_method_relationshipaction_method_relationship or any of its subtypes.

The function returns TRUE if no cycle has been detected. Otherwise it returns FALSE.NOTE 1Note 14.5.1, Note 1
The algorithm of the function is explained in annex E.2. NOTE 2Note 24.5.1, Note 2
This function is not used in this schema. It is defined here because other ISO 10303 integrated resources and application protocols that use the action_method_relationshipaction_method_relationship entity include rules that use this function.
